title: Embedding one-sided subshifts
exact_target: Find exact criteria for embedding a lower-entropy one-sided subshift into a mixing one-sided finite-type shift.
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
A one-sided subshift is a closed set $S\subset A^{\mathbb N_0}$ over
a finite alphabet with $\sigma(S)\subset S$, where $(\sigma x)_n=x_{n+1}$.
Its entropy is $h(S)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\log|\mathcal L_n(S)|$,
with $\mathcal L_n(S)$ the occurring words of length $n$.
Let $T\subset B^{\mathbb N_0}$ be a mixing one-sided shift of finite
type: finitely many forbidden words define $T$, and for any allowed
words all sufficiently long connecting lengths are possible.
Assume $h(S)<h(T)$.

Give useful necessary and sufficient conditions for an embedding
$\iota:S\to T$ to exist. An embedding is a continuous injective map
satisfying $\iota\sigma_S=\sigma_T\iota$; compactness makes it a
conjugacy from $S$ onto its image subshift. Its local coding rule
may use a finite amount of future information, with no past
coordinates available.

Any such map injects periodic orbits of each least period and embeds
the backward preimage tree of a point of $S$ into that of its image
in $T$. Thus entropy alone cannot decide the embedding question.
The desired criterion must handle these compatibility restrictions
throughout the one-sided system. No finite-type or sofic hypothesis
is imposed on $S$, and no coding radius is specified in advance.
All embeddings must preserve one shift step, rather than only an
iterate or an orbit relation.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Find exact criteria for embedding a lower-entropy one-sided subshift into a mixing one-sided finite-type shift.
